items.reason: R4 names IL-12 given to support a vaccine as part of the excluded therapy. Here 'Fusion cells will be administered with IL-12 to enhance the immunity of patients'; IL-12 has no own arm and the only immune outcome assesses 'serial vaccination with DC/Tumor Fusion Cells and IL-12' jointly, so the R4 exception (tested in its own right) does not apply.

IL-12 is the vaccine's immune enhancer ('Dendritic and Glioma Cells Fusion vaccine given with IL-12'), not a separately tested antitumour agent; the coders' analogy to 'pembrolizumab + vaccine' predates R4, which now governs cytokines given with vaccines.

With IL-12 not a candidate the trial has no eligible candidate, so regimen is not_applicable and no partners are recorded. If XL keeps IL-12 as a candidate, use A's list (the vaccine is a DC/tumour fusion vaccine).

note: Proposal overturns both coders' agreed inclusion at S6 by applying D30-R4 (IL-12 given 'to enhance the immunity' of the DC/tumour fusion vaccine), which D31-B8 confirms as part of the excluded therapy; no remaining open question for XL. target_engagement_planned proposed 'no' (coders: yes) because the immune assays measure vaccine-induced immunity and there is no candidate. If XL instead treats IL-12 as tested in its own right, revert to the coders' coding: IL-12 experimental_monotherapy, regimen combination, target_engagement yes.
